editorial:
Imagine moving to a quiet farming town in the 1970s to start a family, only to find out the neighborhood has a dark secret. You follow a Mexican-American couple who are excited about their first baby, but things get weird fast. The wife starts seeing scary things and feeling sick, and she can't tell if she is losing her mind or if a local curse is actually real. It feels like a slow burn that builds up a lot of tension, making you feel just as confused and scared as the main character is throughout the story.

The acting is solid and makes the fear feel real, though some parts of the plot move a bit slowly. You will love the creepy atmosphere and the way it mixes family drama with supernatural scares. If you enjoy movies that keep you guessing until the very end, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: You find out that the scary visions were part of a dark cycle. The twist is that the local community was involved in a ritual to protect their land and children. The main character realizes she is being targeted by a supernatural force tied to the mothers who came before her. In the end, she has to fight off the curse to save her unborn baby, leading to a tense showdown that reveals the true evil hiding in the town.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves folk horror and family mysteries.
